operations_plan.summary: Create a new hollow cylindrical bearing boss on the square, non-filleted end of the arm. Interpret the mounting location as the broad top face adjacent to the terminal face at x=80, centered across the arm width at y=17, with the bearing axis normal to the broad face along Z. Match the existing bearing's nominal outer radius 7, bore radius 5, and socket depth/axial length 9. The exact root-blend profile is not specified, so use a tangent load-spreading blend comparable to the existing boss without changing the remaining arm profile.

steps.description: Identify the requested non-filleted end as the rectangular terminal face at x=80 (face 7), opposite the rounded negative-X terminal (face 0). Use the adjacent broad top plate face at z=6 (face 6) as the bearing mounting face. Preserve the terminal face, rounded end, plate thickness, existing pivot boss, and all other original geometry except for the local union and blend required by the new bearing.

Create a sketch on the top plate plane z=6, using face 6 as the support and face 7 as the end-location reference. Place the bearing center at x=80 and at the midpoint of the strip width, y=(11+23)/2=17. Constrain the center coincident with the projected x=80 terminal boundary and centered between the y=11 and y=23 sidewalls. Define the bearing axis through this point normal to the sketch plane, parallel to +Z. This axis-direction choice follows the aim's preferred interpretation; mounting directly on face 7 with an X-directed axis remains an unresolved alternative in the source wording.

Sketch an outer circle of radius 7 centered on the new Z-axis, matching the radius-7 outer wall of the existing boss (face 10). Additively extrude the circular profile 9 units from z=6 toward +Z, producing a cylindrical boss that terminates at z=15. Fuse the extrusion to original solid 0 through the portion of its footprint supported by the top plate near x=80; do not extend or reshape the arm itself.

On the new boss's top circular face at z=15, sketch a concentric circle of radius 5, matching the existing socket wall radius represented by face 3. Subtractively extrude the circle 9 units toward -Z and stop at z=6. This creates a blind cylindrical socket with a planar floor coincident with the original top-face level, an annular entrance rim, 2-unit nominal radial wall thickness, and an axis coincident with the axis established in step 2. Do not cut through the 4-unit-thick arm plate.

Create a tangent root fillet or smooth blend where the new outer cylindrical wall intersects the top plate, analogous in function to the existing BSpline boss root on face 9. Limit the blend to the local supported junction and select the largest manufacturable radius that does not enter the radius-5 bore, remove the 2-unit wall, or modify the distant arm boundaries. Because no blend radius is specified and the existing BSpline cannot be uniquely reconstructed from the supplied metadata, treat the exact blend dimensions as unresolved and prioritize a valid smooth union. Verify that the resulting bearing remains coaxial, has outer radius 7, inner radius 5, a 9-unit blind depth, and is part of the same solid as the arm.

operations_plan.summary: Create seven additional rotational instances of the completed seed design around the axis of the new flat-end bearing, giving eight total equally spaced instances over 360 degrees. Interpret 'this design' as the entire completed part—including the arm, original transverse socket boss, and newly added bearing—because patterning only the axisymmetric new bearing around its own axis would create coincident, visually unchanged copies.

steps.description: Use the center axis of the newly created radius-5/radius-7 bearing as the circular-pattern axis. The axis passes through global point (80,17,6) and is directed along Z. Select the complete post-operation_001 solid as the seed body, including section_arm, section_pivot_boss, and section_new_flat_end_bearing. Preserve the seed instance at its original zero-degree orientation.

Apply a full circular body pattern with 8 total occurrences, comprising the original seed plus 7 additional instances. Set the total angular extent to 360 degrees and equal spacing to 45 degrees. Generate instances at 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, and 315 degrees about the new bearing's Z-axis. This full-circle equal-spacing definition is inferred because the request specifies seven additional instances but does not provide a partial angle or increment.

Resolve the coincident central bearing geometry produced by rotating the complete seed about its own new bearing axis. Boolean-union coincident and intersecting patterned occurrences where possible so the eight radial arms share one common central bearing, while retaining all eight rotated arms and all eight copies of the original transverse pivot boss. If the target CAD system maintains patterned bodies as separate occurrences, keep them as an eight-occurrence patterned assembly but suppress duplicate coincident central-bearing bodies from mass-property double counting.

Validate the final radial design: confirm eight geometrically identical arm instances at 45-degree increments, a common pattern axis coincident with the new bearing bore, unchanged 4-unit arm thickness and original arm profiles within every occurrence, preserved existing radius-7/radius-5 blind pivot sockets, and no unintended cuts or failed unions at the central patterned region. Confirm that the new central bearing bore remains open and cylindrically continuous after pattern consolidation.
